reasoning: The test uses `page.request.post()` (Playwright's APIRequestContext) to call `/themes/<slug>/default` to restore the original default theme. The Flask application has CSRF protection enabled via `security.py` — the `before_request` hook blocks all unsafe (POST/PUT/DELETE) requests that lack a valid `X-CSRF-Token` header. Browser-side `fetch` and htmx requests automatically include this token via `security.js` (which intercepts `window.fetch` and the `htmx:configRequest` event), but `page.request.post()` is a raw HTTP API call that bypasses the browser JavaScript layer entirely. The POST receives a 403 Forbidden response, but the test never inspects the response status, so it silently proceeds. The theme default is never restored server-side, and the final assertion at line 212 (`toHaveAttribute('data-theme', originalDefault)`) fails because the test theme remains the active default. The same silent-failure pattern affects `deleteThemeViaApi` but other tests don't verify its effect, so they pass despite not actually cleaning up. The skipped `themes_delete_custom_theme` test avoids this issue by using UI interactions (which go through htmx and include the CSRF token).
suggestedAction: Fix `page.request.post()` calls to include the CSRF token header. Extract the token via `await page.evaluate(() => window.APP_CONFIG.csrfToken)` and pass it as `{ headers: { 'X-CSRF-Token': csrfToken } }` in all `page.request.post()` options. Apply this to: (1) the default-restore POST in `themes_set_default_theme` finally block, (2) the `deleteThemeViaApi` helper function, and (3) the `afterAll` cleanup hook (which must first navigate to a page to obtain the token).
